clauses.current_legal_basis: Executive Order 13808 of August 24, 2017 (82 FR 41155) took additional steps under the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692 of March 8, 2015, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. That emergency was continued by notice every year from 2018 through 2026; the held Notice of February 18, 2026 (91 FR 8357, FR Doc. 2026-03502) continues it for one year and names Executive Order 13808 among the orders that took additional steps under it. The held Federal Register texts of every executive order numbered 13809 through 14435 (14435 was signed 2026-10-05) were scanned for this order's number; the only order that cites it with a changing verb is Executive Order 13857, which amended subsection (d) of section 3 (listed as a later event on that clause). Orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are not held and are covered only by the catalog search. Executive Order 14373 of January 9, 2026 (91 FR 2045) declares a separate national emergency about Foreign Government Deposit Funds and supersedes earlier executive orders only to the extent they block, regulate or otherwise affect those funds; it does not name this order, and no clause of this order addresses funds held by the United States Treasury on behalf of the Government of Venezuela, so it is not treated as ending any clause. The Federal Register executive-order catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog, checked 2026-11-25) shows only Executive Order 13857's amendment of subsection (d) of section 3, and the eCFR search (current-law:ecfr) shows regulations implementing the order. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1(a) prohibits United States persons and persons within the United States from transactions in, financing for, and other dealings in the debt, equity, bonds and dividend payments described in paragraphs (i) through (iv). The prohibitions continue: no held instrument revokes or narrows them, and the order is unamended in this clause. This clause depends on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692; the yearly continuation notices are recorded as later events on section 1 of this order and are not ends.

clauses.reason: Section 3(d) defines the Government of Venezuela, which fixes the reach of the prohibitions in section 1. Executive Order 13857 of January 25, 2019 (84 FR 509), section 1(a), amended subsection (d) of section 3 to read as follows: the term Government of Venezuela includes the state and Government of Venezuela, any political subdivision, agency or instrumentality (including the Central Bank of Venezuela and Petroleos de Venezuela, S.A.), any person owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by them, and any person who has acted or purported to act for or on behalf of any of them, including as a member of the Maduro regime. Before the amendment the definition covered the Government of Venezuela, its subdivisions, agencies and instrumentalities (including the Central Bank and PdVSA) and any person owned or controlled by, or acting for or on behalf of, the Government of Venezuela. The amended definition is broader, so the substance changed. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert and restated provisions, the clause continues, amended, until its parent order ends; this order has not ended. Reviewer note: the current wording of this definition is the 2019 wording, not the wording printed in the original order. The prohibitions it defines continue.

Executive Order 13808 (82 FR 41155, signed 2017-08-24, published 2017-08-29, FR Doc. 2017-18468) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13808.txt, the registered official original. The order is emergency-dependent: it rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13692, which the President continued by notice each year from 2018 through 2026 (nine held notices, recorded as later events on section 1; the last, signed February 18, 2026, runs to March 2027, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14). No instrument revokes or supersedes the order or any other clause. Executive Order 13827, Executive Order 13835, Executive Order 13850 and Executive Order 13857 cite it as an earlier step without revoking it. Executive Order 14245 of March 24, 2025 (90 FR 13829), section 1(b), states that existing sanctions on Venezuela, including those imposed in Executive Order 13808, remain in effect; it is recorded as a later event on section 1, and it neither amends nor ends the order. savings.reason: Executive Order 13808 has no savings or transition clause: section 1(c) preserves the prohibitions notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits, and section 6 only disclaims private rights. The amendment by Executive Order 13857 changes the definition in section 3(d) without saving or transferring any right or action from the original wording, and the bounded searches found no instrument that would do so.
